kb.name: Lumora Ledger product overview
kb.content: Lumora Ledger is an accounts-payable automation product from Fernhollow Software. It captures invoices from email and PDF, extracts header and line-item fields, and runs three-way matching against purchase orders and goods receipts. It is built for mid-market finance teams processing 1,000 to 50,000 invoices per month. Native integrations: Corvel ERP, Brightbook Accounts and Tallyhouse. On Fernhollow's 2025 internal benchmark of 12,000 invoices, field-level extraction accuracy was 96%. Approval routing supports up to five approval tiers.

kb.name: Case study: Quarry & Pine Outfitters
kb.content: Quarry & Pine Outfitters, a 300-person outdoor retailer, rolled out Lumora Ledger in 2025. Average invoice processing time fell from 9 days to 3 days. Late-payment fees fell 62% over the first two quarters after go-live. The AP team stayed at three people while invoice volume grew.

kb.name: Case study: Harbor Thistle Foods
kb.content: Harbor Thistle Foods, a regional food distributor, processes about 14,000 invoices per month in Lumora Ledger with a four-person AP team. Invoices needing manual exception review dropped to 8% of volume.

kb.name: Security and compliance
kb.content: Lumora Ledger has a SOC 2 Type II report, audited annually by an independent firm. Customer data is encrypted with AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2 or higher in transit. Production runs in a US East region and an EU West region, and customers choose the region. ISO 27001 certification is in progress and has not been achieved. Lumora Ledger is not HIPAA compliant and is not FedRAMP authorized.

kb.name: Pricing and rollout
kb.content: Lumora Ledger pricing starts at $1,800 per month, which covers up to 2,000 invoices per month. Typical implementation takes six weeks. Prospects can run a 30-day pilot on their own invoices before signing.

kb.name: Scale plan pricing
kb.content: Lumora Ledger Scale plan pricing starts at $4,200 per month, which covers up to 10,000 invoices per month. Typical implementation on the Scale plan takes ten weeks. Scale customers get a named support engineer and a 99.5% uptime commitment in the service agreement.

kb.name: Identity and access
kb.content: Identity and access. Lumora Ledger supports SSO through SAML 2.0 with Keystone ID and Lanternpass. SSO is included on the Scale plan only and is not available on the $1,800 starting plan. SCIM provisioning is on the roadmap and is not yet available. Every account enforces MFA for administrators. Role-based access control (RBAC) ships with four built-in roles: Admin, Approver, Clerk and Auditor.

kb.name: ERP connectors
kb.content: ERP connectors. Native two-way connectors exist for Corvel ERP, Brightbook Accounts and Tallyhouse. Approved invoices post to the ERP as payable bills, and payment status syncs from the ERP every 15 minutes. Nettlefield ERP is supported through a nightly CSV file exchange only; there is no API connector for Nettlefield. Lumora Ledger reads the vendor master from the ERP and never creates vendors in the ERP.

kb.name: Limits and unsupported uses
kb.content: Limits and unsupported uses. Lumora Ledger does not support on-premises deployment; it runs only as a cloud service. It does not pay suppliers in cryptocurrency. There is no mobile app; approvers use the web app or approve from email. It does not process payroll, employee expenses or corporate cards. It does not create purchase orders, so POs must already exist in the ERP.

kb.name: Implementation and support handbook
kb.content:
Lumora Ledger implementation and support handbook. This handbook describes how Fernhollow Software onboards new customers and supports them after go-live. It is written for finance leaders and IT owners who are planning a rollout. Each rollout has three phases: connect, configure and go live. The handbook covers who does what in each phase, what Fernhollow needs from the customer, and how support works once the system is in daily use. Read it together with the pricing sheet.

Connect phase. In the first phase the customer's IT owner grants read access to the ERP and sets up the invoice inbox. Fernhollow's onboarding team imports the vendor master and the last 90 days of purchase orders so that matching can start on day one. Customers who use a scanning bureau for paper invoices can route the scanned PDFs into the same inbox. Fernhollow asks for one named finance owner and one named IT owner for the whole rollout.

Configure phase. During configuration the finance owner sets approval rules, tolerance thresholds for price and quantity differences, and the GL coding defaults. The default matching tolerance is 2% or $50 per invoice line, whichever is lower, and customers can change it. Fernhollow runs a parallel test in which every invoice is processed both in the old process and in Lumora Ledger for two weeks before go-live.

Support after go-live. Standard support runs 24 hours a day, five days a week, by email and in-app chat. Priority-one incidents, meaning invoices cannot be captured or approved, have a first-response target of one hour. All other tickets have a first-response target of one business day. Phone support is not offered. Customers processing more than 5,000 invoices a month are assigned a customer success manager who runs a quarterly business review.

Data retention and exit. Invoice images and extracted data are retained for seven years by default, which meets most audit requirements, and can be set to a shorter period on request. If a customer leaves, Fernhollow exports all invoice images and data as PDF and CSV files within 30 days of the request, and then deletes the customer's data within a further 30 days. Backups are encrypted and kept for 35 days.
